"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Forming coalitions and cooperative security arrangements is key to confronting emerging transnational threats.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[2]},{"claim_text":"Support for President Bush's leadership in the establishment of a consensus among the G-8 nations to support peacekeeping capabilities among the nations of Africa.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[3]},{"claim_text":"With increased peacekeeping capabilities, African nations may more effectively prevent and resolve violent conflict on the continent.",

"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[4]},{"claim_text":"The Bush Administration has helped achieve progress toward resolving conflicts in Liberia, Angola, the Democratic Republic of Congo, Sierra Leone, and Sudan, working in concert with allies, friends, and international institutions.",
